Cc: partner@cloudbridge.io, procurement@signalworks.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T15:12:00Z
Subject: Private Offer for SignalWorks — tiered SKU & channel margin proposal

Hi Grace,

Following our call this morning, AWS is prepared to draft a private offer for SignalWorks. They are looking for a two-tier commitment: a 12-month initial commit at $120k/mo (tier A) and an optional growth tier for months 13-24 at $200k/mo (tier B) with blended discounts applied to marketplace SKUs.

Key asks from AWS/SignalWorks:
- SignalWorks wants a marketplace-deliverable private offer so they can use existing procurement flows.
- CloudBridge (reseller) needs a channel margin carved out of the effective discount; they asked for visibility into our suggested split.
- Clarify whether Dedicated Reserved SKUs (Dedicated GPU pools) can be offered via the marketplace private offer or if they must be excluded/signed off separately.

I've attached a draft private-offer PDF with the AWS-side fields filled. Can you confirm:
1) a recommended Redwood list price / marketplace SKU mapping for the two tiers (hosted vs dedicated),
2) what channel margin% we are willing to grant to CloudBridge for this deal, and
3) any constraints on committing Dedicated capacity via a marketplace PO?

If we can get a finalized pricing sheet this week AWS can push the private-offer through their portal and SignalWorks can route to procurement.

Attachments: AWS_PrivateOffer_Draft_SignalWorks.pdf

Thanks,
Leslie Chen
AWS Strategic Accounts — Marketplace

Team — forwarding Leslie's note (below). SignalWorks is pushing to keep the PO on-marketplace. They want a single private-offer that covers both hosted API and a Dedicated reserved component if possible. CloudBridge will expect a reseller commission.

Quick asks from our side before I reply to Leslie:
- Priyom: can you draft an initial SKU mapping and suggested list prices for tier A and B (hosted per-token vs dedicated per-reserved-unit)? See attached sketch (sku-proposal.csv).
- Marcus: finance needs to weigh in on partner margin floor (what minimum commission we can give without eroding blended ASP).
- Karthik: any technical/legal constraints on including Dedicated Reserved SKUs in an AWS private-offer? I recall marketplace is picky about long-term reserved capacity.

I think a workable starting point is: 18% gross discount to SignalWorks at tier A, 22% at tier B, with a 10% reseller commission on the incremental discount. But that's a gut — want numbers from finance.

Please reply with redlines by EOD tomorrow. Leslie flagged procurement timelines (they want PO in AWS portal this week if possible).

From: priyom_das@redwood.com

Date: 2026-12-01T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private Offer for SignalWorks — tiered SKU & channel margin proposal

Thanks Grace — I took a pass on SKU mapping and ran quick margin math. High-level:

Proposal (hosted / dedicated):
- Tier A (12mo commit): Hosted (per-token): list $0.0009/token -> customer effective price after 18% discount = $0.000738/token. Dedicated (reserved-unit): list $9,000/unit/mo -> effective $7,380/unit/mo.
- Tier B (13-24mo growth): Hosted list same -> 22% discount -> $0.000702/token. Dedicated -> $7,020/unit/mo.

Channel split idea: give CloudBridge a 10% commission on Redwood's net revenue (i.e., 10% of the price we actually invoice after discount). That keeps the math simple and avoids stacking discounts on the list price. At those numbers the gross-to-net and our gross margin stay within acceptable ranges for a strategic deal.

Notes / concerns:
- If we allow Dedicated to be purchased via the marketplace private offer, AWS charges marketplace fees and there are limitations on 3rd-party uptime SLAs tied to those SKUs. That could complicate our Dedicated SLA commitments.
- If SignalWorks insists on Dedicated via the PO, we should carve Dedicated into a separate line item with an explicit "managed-by-Redwood (off-market)" clause so we can support our SLA. That means AWS will still process a private offer but the Dedicated commitment is effectively backed by a separate reserved contract we own directly.

I attached the CSV I used for the quick calcs. If finance is comfortable with 10% partner commission I can prepare the priced sheet for AWS.

—Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive — Marketplace
priyom_das@redwood.com
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Private Offer for SignalWorks — margin guidance

Grace / Priyom — quick finance perspective.

We ran the blended P&L for the proposed tiers. Summary:
- 18% discount (Tier A) / 22% discount (Tier B) is acceptable but leaves limited room for >12% reseller commission.
- Recommend capping reseller commission at 10% of Redwood net revenue as Priyom suggested. That yields an acceptable blended gross margin (approx 48% blended across hosted+dedicated) for a strategic win.

Process guidance:
1) Approve final list-to-customer pricing (I need the priced sheet).
2) We will issue internal approval memo for discounts >15% (this one needs that).
3) If Dedicated is included in-marketplace, legal needs to add the SLA carve-out language. I recommend we keep Dedicated as an off-market managed SKU and only include hosted in the AWS private-offer invoiceable lines.

I attached a redlined PO terms doc with suggested language for "Dedicated capacity managed off-market" and a clause for partner commission payments (PO-based rebate quarterly). If Sales approves I can finalize the memo and route to pricing-approval mailing list.

Attachment: PO_Terms_redlined.pdf

Marcus Lin
Head of Finance Ops — Revenue

Grace / Team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed mechanics. AWS can implement a private offer that enumerates hosted SKUs with the Tier A / Tier B pricing and an off-market carve-out line for the Dedicated reserved component. That mirrors Marcus' suggestion and should keep your SLA obligations clean.

Next steps I need from Redwood:
- Finalized pricing spreadsheet (hosted SKU rows filled, Tier A & B prices, and explicit reseller commission percent).
- Confirmation you want CloudBridge paid as a reseller commission via quarterly rebate (yes/no). If yes, provide the legal remit address for CloudBridge.
- Confirmation to proceed with the DocuSign PO flow. If so, I'll create the private offer in AWS Marketplace and link the DocuSign packet to the SignalWorks procurement contact.

We can keep the Dedicated "managed off-market" line as a note in the offer; AWS will accept that but it will be marked "non-billable" in Marketplace and must be billed separately by Redwood. Make sure your legal team signs off.

I'll hold the offer draft until I receive the pricing sheet and CloudBridge remit. If you can send today, we can hit SignalWorks procurement SLA.
